question: You are permitted to use the outer most right lane on a three-lane dual carriageway when

options.text: You are travelling at the maximum legal speed limit of the road.
You intend to turn right ahead.
Emergency vehicles are not using it.

notes: 'outer most' is printed as two words in the source.

question: When the temperature gauge on your vehicle indicates 'hot'. What is the cause?

options.text: The exhaust pipe is getting too hot.
The engine is heating up.
The air conditioning is not working properly.

question: While driving, and your engine gets overheated , you should

options.text: Pour water to cool down the engine.
Slow down and stop at a safe spot to let the engine cool down by itself.
Drive to the nearest petrol kiosk for repairs.

notes: Source has a space before the comma after 'overheated'.

question: You are driving in very wet weather. Your vehicle begins to slide. This effect is called

options.text: Weaving.
Fading.
Aquaplaning.

question: You are travelling at the legal speed limit. A vehicle comes up quickly behind, flashing its headlights. You should

options.text: Maintain your speed to prevent the vehicle from overtaking.
Allow the vehicle to overtake.
Touch the brakes sharply to show your brake lights.

question: What should you use the road shoulder of an expressway for?

options.text: Leaving the expressway.
Joining the expressway.
Stopping in an emergency.

question: You intend to turn left and there is a cyclist ahead on the left, you should

options.text: Slow down and allow the cyclist to pass the junction.
Drive faster to avoid the cyclist.
Horn to warn him you are turning left.

question: You should never attempt to overtake a cyclist

options.text: Just before you turn left.
Just before you turn right.
On a one-way street.

question: You should use your right hand indicator when

options.text: You intend to slow down.
You are about to stop.
You intend to move to the right at any time.

question: You should check your mirrors before

options.text: Moving off, slowing down and stopping.
Changing lane, overtaking, turning and every 5 to 10 seconds.
Both A and B.

notes: Option C refers to options A and B.

question: When driving behind a bus, you should

options.text: Keep a longer following distance.
Keep the normal following distance.
Keep more to the right to have a better view.

question: When you are driving along a main road, you should

options.text: Stop at every road junction before proceeding.
Accelerate through each junction.
Check every side road before you drive past them.

question: You notice a vehicle trying to pull out between a row of stationary vehicles. You should

options.text: Drive on regardless of danger ahead.
Sound the horn and maintain your speed.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: As vehicle speed increases, your field of vision would be

options.text: Reduced.
Remained the same.
Increased.

notes: Option B 'Remained the same.' is ungrammatical in the source; kept as printed.

question: When driving, your arms should be

options.text: Straighten.
Slightly bent.
Bent at 90 degree.

notes: Source wording 'Straighten.' and '90 degree' kept as printed.

question: Some of the common vehicle defects that can cause accidents are

options.text: Faulty seat belts, seats, child restraint and alarm system.
Faulty tyres, brakes, shock absorbers and windscreen wipers.
Dull paint, dented bumpers and old seats.

question: The handbrake of a car acts

options.text: Only on the rear wheels.
Only on the front wheels.
On both the front and rear wheels.

question: When passing the stationary bus at the bus-stop, you should
picture: Video frame: red bus stopped in a yellow-marked bus bay with people at the stop, white car on the road

options.text: Sound the horn to warn the bus driver of your presence.
Speed up to overtake the bus before it moves off.
Slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrian who may cross the road in front of the bus.

notes: Picture panel is a video frame with a Repeat Video button. 'bus-' / 'stop' wraps across a line break, joined as 'bus-stop'. Option C 'for pedestrian' (singular, no article) kept as printed.

question: Both the van and the car are entering a car park, the car should not overtake the van
picture: Top-down video frame: white van, red car, road with double yellow lines and white centre line, car park on right

options.text: Because of the centre white line.
Because of the double yellow line.
Because it is not safe to do so.

notes: Picture panel is a video frame with a Repeat Video button.

question: How does alcohol affect you?

options.text: It reduces your concentration.
It increases your awareness.
It improves your co-ordination.
